historical_references.reference: Gitali is a common female name in Hindu communities, particularly in the state of Bengal, India. It is derived from the Sanskrit word 'git' meaning 'music' or 'song'. The name may have originated from the Hindu goddess of music, Saraswati, who is often depicted holding a veena, a musical instrument. In ancient Indian texts, the goddess is also referred to as 'Gita-Ratna', or the 'jewel of songs'.

Another possible origin of the name Gitali is from the Hindu epic, the Mahabharata. In the epic, there is a character named Gitala, who is the wife of the great sage Vyasa. Vyasa is the author of the Mahabharata and is also known as the incarnation of Lord God Vishnu. Gitala is described as a beautiful and virtuous woman who helps her husband in writing the great epic. The name Gitali may be derived from the Sanskrit word 'gita', meaning 'song', which may refer to the fact that Vyasa's epic is a collection of songs and narratives.
